E1.note: class A demo example: one table (payments), 1 row inserted; ops lead may approve
E1.sql: INSERT INTO payments (invoice_id, amount_cents, paid_on, method, kind, refund_of) SELECT invoice_id, amount_cents, DATE '2026-11-01', method, 'refund', id FROM payments WHERE id = 2565

E2.sql: UPDATE accounts SET balance_cents = (SELECT coalesce(sum(amount_cents - paid_cents), 0) FROM invoices WHERE account_id = 7 AND status = 'open') WHERE id = 7

E5.sql: WITH closed AS (UPDATE accounts SET status = 'closed' WHERE customer_id = 201 AND id <> (SELECT id FROM accounts WHERE customer_id = 201 ORDER BY opened_on, id LIMIT 1) RETURNING id) UPDATE subscriptions SET status = 'cancelled' WHERE status = 'active' AND account_id IN (SELECT id FROM closed)

E6.sql: UPDATE subscriptions SET monthly_cents = round(monthly_cents * 0.9) WHERE plan = 'enterprise' AND status = 'active'

E8.sql: WITH w AS (UPDATE invoices SET status = 'written_off' WHERE status = 'open' AND due_on <= DATE '2026-11-01' - 90 AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment_plans p WHERE p.invoice_id = invoices.id AND p.status = 'active') RETURNING account_id, amount_cents - paid_cents AS owed) UPDATE accounts a SET balance_cents = a.balance_cents - s.owed FROM (SELECT account_id, sum(owed) AS owed FROM w GROUP BY account_id) s WHERE a.id = s.account_id
E8.naive_sql: UPDATE invoices SET status = 'written_off' WHERE status = 'open' AND due_on <= DATE '2026-11-01' - 90

E11.metric_note: re-sums all three metrics (api_call, seat_day, gb_stored), not only seat_day: the stored total is one figure, so every metric is recomputed
E11.sql: UPDATE accounts a SET usage_cents_oct = (SELECT coalesce(sum(u.amount_cents), 0) FROM usage_events u WHERE u.account_id = a.id AND u.occurred_at >= DATE '2026-10-01' AND u.occurred_at < DATE '2026-11-01')
